summary: Today’s pulse tracks Watch as fire engulfs Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat, Ukraine’s military says Starlink satellite connection stable after recent restrictions, and Thousands march in Paris and other French cities as protests take place across Europe – Europe live. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are northern, fender, and military. In the background, Sam Fender tells fans high ticket prices for Proper Massive tour are ‘getting changed’ and Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Watch as fire engulfs Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
headlines.description: Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a 33-year-old German man following the fire.

headlines.title: Ukraine’s military says Starlink satellite connection stable after recent restrictions
headlines.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy offers thanks to US allies for restoring system key to air defence and ‘frontline logistics’ Ukraine’s military has a “stable connection to Starlink”, the Ukrainian government has said, 10 days after its ability to use the satellite communications system was suddenly restricted . The Starlink satellite terminals, which are produced by Elon Musk’s SpaceX but managed by the US government, are a key component of Ukraine’s military operations. Sudden speed restrictions on the terminals, which capped operations at speeds of 160km/h (99mph), led to the failure of several Ukrainian combat missions earlier this month.

headlines.title: Thousands march in Paris and other French cities as protests take place across Europe – Europe live
headlines.description: French police have made 135 arrests, while Italian officers have raided homes in Milan, with protests also taking place in Spain and Albania Jesse, 40, a charity worker from the north of Paris, had turned out for the street march. She said: “I’m so angry. I’m here to support schoolchildren’s demands for better conditions. I’m so proud of them and we have to stand together.”

headlines.title: Sam Fender tells fans high ticket prices for Proper Massive tour are ‘getting changed’
headlines.description: Fender criticises stadium pricing, calling it ‘bollocks’ and says it ‘won’t be happening’ on his tour Sam Fender has responded to criticism by fans about ticket prices for his 2027 stadium tour by promising he would lower the cost, telling followers on Instagram: “They’re getting changed.” The 32-year-old musician announced his Proper Massive stadium tour earlier this week.

headlines.title: Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
headlines.description: Some 200 emergency personnel were deployed to fight the blaze at the Nazi dictator's Alpine residence in Germany.

headlines.title: Northern Olympics campaign to get £7m in Healey’s budget
headlines.description: Fund will support feasibility study for potential bid to host Games in 2040s, backed by northern mayors and top athletes John Healey is to announce a £7m fund to examine a potential future bid to host the Olympics in northern England in his first budget as chancellor. The fund will be used to carry out a full feasibility study for a northern Games, which, if successful, would be held in the north of England in the 2040s.

headlinePool.title: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
headlinePool.description: The ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr, with whom she shares five children, announced in May that she had been diagnosed with breast cancer.

headlinePool.title: Suspect arrested over fire at Hitler’s ‘Eagle’s Nest’ retreat in Bavaria
headlinePool.description: About 200 firefighters deployed to tackle blaze at former Nazi mountain retreat in remote part of southern Germany Police have arrested a 33-year-old German citizen after a fire ripped through Adolf Hitler’s former mountain retreat in Bavaria, leaving the historic Nazi meeting place – known as the Eagle’s Nest – largely destroyed. About 200 firefighters were deployed on Friday night to tackle the blaze at the Nazi dictator’s remote, purpose-built Kehlsteinhaus residence, a protected building on the peak of Obersalzberg in southern Germany.

headlinePool.title: Nine killed and 40 injured after gunmen open fire at church funeral in Jordan
headlinePool.description: Footage broadcast on state TV shows three attackers approaching Greek Orthodox church and firing shots Nine people have been killed after gunmen opened fire at a funeral at a church in Jordan in a rare attack ⁠on the country’s Christian minority. Authorities described the attack on Friday as a terrorist act by extremists.

headlinePool.title: Met says it shared allegations about Meghan’s father with her but not other forces
headlinePool.description: Scotland Yard says it shared letter about Thomas Markle Sr allegations in 2019 but did not pass claims to other agencies The Metropolitan police have confirmed they gave a letter to the Duchess of Sussex in 2019 concerning “alleged offending” involving her father, after accusations arose on Friday about Thomas Markle Sr having child sexual abuse images. Scotland Yard said it had received a letter in January 2019 making a number of allegations about offending outside Britain.

headlinePool.title: Kim Jong-un crosses newly opened bridge into China
headlinePool.description: North Korean leader travels over New Yalu River Bridge to meet senior Communist party member Kim Jong-un has visited China, inaugurating a bridge that connects the two countries and saying he hopes to expand cooperation with his neighbour. The North Korean leader arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday after crossing the New Yalu River Bridge, according to South Korea’s unification ministry, which handles affairs related to North Korea, and China’s official Xinhua news agency.

headlinePool.title: Storm Boelo to bring 80mph gusts and heavy rain to parts of UK
headlinePool.description: Second named storm will hit northern parts of UK as thousands remain without power after Friday’s Storm Austen The UK is bracing for a second storm this weekend, as strong winds and heavy rain are expected to disrupt travel and cause further power cuts in the north. Storm Boelo, the second named storm of the season, is expected to bring heavy, frequent showers and winds potentially exceeding 80mph to northern parts of the UK.

headlinePool.title: Israeli soldiers raze neighbourhood in Hebron, driving families from homes
headlinePool.description: PM Benjamin Netanyahu vows ‘to destroy this place’ in retaliation for militant attack on army checkpoint Israeli troops have levelled a neighbourhood in Hebron, driving out hundreds of families in collective punishment for a militant attack on an army checkpoint outside the West Bank city, local Palestinian authorities said. The Hebron municipality estimated that 35 hectares (86 acres) had been destroyed or marked for destruction and about 1,500 people had been evicted from their homes by Saturday afternoon in the district of Ein Deir Baha. The whole city of 250,000 people was sealed off by checkpoints on every point of entry.

headlinePool.title: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
headlinePool.description: The slowed Starlink connections had affected the Ukraine's military and drone operations for a week.

headlinePool.title: Additional 178 cases of measles reported by US health authorities amid outbreak
headlinePool.description: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 4,588 cases across the country, more than double the tally in 2025 Federal health authorities reported an additional 178 cases of measles in the US this week, as the vaccine-preventable illness continues to sicken people across at least 43 outbreaks. The new data reported by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) comes as experts criticize the agency for lack of transparency, and as health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr takes steps to further upend US vaccine infrastructure.
